chosen.title: The Warning That Never Came: How OpenAI's PR Team Overruled Its Own Safety Engineers
chosen.rationale: Breaking right now (Sept 2-3, 2026): 30 new civil complaints allege OpenAI's safety team recommended referring a user's violent ChatGPT conversations to police before the Tumbler Ridge school shooting, and that global-affairs/PR leadership overrode them and stayed silent, invoking 'aiding and abetting' liability. It's the exact Arendtian banality-of-complicity, image-over-accountability story Dawn owns, and distinct from AIMA's existing 'courts ended the accountability holiday' piece because the hook is the internal corporate decision, not the courtroom outcome.

sources.name: NPR — New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety
Bloomberg Law — OpenAI Faces New Lawsuits Linked to Shooting at Canadian School
Al Jazeera — Families sue OpenAI, alleging chatbot aided in Canadian school shooting

rejected_candidates.title: Guilty Until Audited: How Welfare-Fraud Algorithms Turned Poverty Into Probable Cause
rejected_candidates.rationale: A live 2026 thread — the April 2026 'Holes in the Public Record' paper shows welfare-adjudication algorithms are buried so claimants can't even prove one touched their case, while Sweden's fraud model was found to discriminate against women, migrants, and low-income claimants. Pure Dawn: follow-the-money, data colonialism, bureaucracy-as-violence, and a harm that lands only on people without lawyers. Not covered by AIMA's insurance/eviction/résumé pieces, which target different systems.

The Conversation — AI algorithms intended to root out welfare fraud often end up punishing the poor

rejected_candidates.title: Whose Outbreak Counts: AI Disease Surveillance and the New Data Colonialism
rejected_candidates.rationale: A cluster of Sept 2026 reviews (Frontiers, Lancet Regional Health, and an AJPH call flagged via EurekAlert) warn AI disease surveillance is outpacing governance — trusting hospital/lab data while dismissing community-generated data as 'noise,' entrenching bias against Indigenous, migrant, and low-resource populations. It's Dawn's feminist/postcolonial-critique-of-tech and surveillance beat applied to global public health, an angle none of AIMA's clinical-medicine pieces ('Healing Machine,' 'Diagnosis by Algorithm') touch.

sources.name: Frontiers in Digital Health — AI is transforming disease surveillance, but governance is failing to keep pace
